n_samples_note: post-burnin logged samples pooled across chains (10% burnin per chain); MCMC states per chain = 2.5e6
notes: Likelihood: BDMM-Prime BirthDeathMigrationDistribution (Kuehnert et al. 2016 ODE likelihood, integrated over unobserved type histories; not a mapped/typed-tree likelihood). Tree FIXED: loaded from tree100.nwk via TreeParser, not in the MCMC state, no tree operators. TreeParser adjustTipHeights=true was required: tips in the Newick differ by up to 3e-6 due to 6-decimal rounding, and BDMM-Prime otherwise does not treat them as rho-sampled (logP=-Inf). conditionOnRoot=true, processLength = root height (no stem). Model: 4 types (tip types from tip_types.tsv), single shared birth rate (LogNormal(0,1) prior), death=0, psi sampling rate=0, rho=1 at present, 12 migration rates (BDMM-Prime forward-time, row-major off-diagonal order from->to) with iid Exponential(mean 0.3) priors, root type frequencies (startTypePriorProbs) estimated with Dirichlet(1,1,1,1). Operators: single-element ScaleOperator on migration rates, scaleAll on migration rates, ScaleOperator on birth rate, DeltaExchange on root freqs. Run: 4 independent chains (seeds 1001-1004) run concurrently, 2.5e6 states each, log every 500, 10% burnin; BDMM-Prime internal parallelize=true (~1.8 cores/chain; host shared with another heavy job). wall_seconds = wall time for all 4 concurrent chains; a single chain alone is ~same speed (~2.2-2.8 ms/state). ESS via arviz 0.x bulk ESS (pooled over chains and for chain 1 alone). Mixing is good: single-chain ESS>2400 for all rates, so ESS>200 would need only ~2e5 states (~10 min single chain). Accuracy caveat: with 100 tips the posteriors are wide and prior-sensitive; all 12 true rates lie inside the 95% HPD, but rates out of rare types (esp. type 3) are essentially prior-dominated (median ~0.21-0.27 vs Exp(0.3) prior median 0.21). Installation: BEAST 2.7.7 Linux tarball (bundled JRE); packagemanager -add into ~/.beast failed (write error), so packages were installed with -dir /home/asm/data/bdmm/pkgs; the package manager also pulled BEAST.base/app 2.7.8 which conflicted with the bundled 2.7.7 and were removed. Run with beast -packagedir /home/asm/data/bdmm/pkgs.
